gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both entries identify the same failed boundary-flux contribution in the mesh-dependent norm: the h^{-1} trace term yields an h^{2r-2} interpolation contribution on nonempty flux boundaries, so the proof cannot support the advertised h^{2r} squared-norm rate. The prediction also gives the corresponding lowest-order failure manifestation.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The theorem and proof incorrectly treat the h^{-1}-weighted boundary normal-trace interpolation term as having the bulk h^{2r} order; the cut-trace estimate instead loses one power of h in the norm, producing h^{2r-2} in the squared estimate for nonempty flux boundaries.

component_coverage.gold_component: Incorrect h^{2r} boundary-flux contribution in the squared mesh-dependent error norm, caused by applying the trace/interpolation estimate without the h-loss on nonempty flux boundaries.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly identifies the h^{-1} boundary term, derives the correct h^{2r-2} scaling rather than h^{2r}, and explains that this prevents the claimed full-norm convergence rate, including the O(1) lowest-order case.
